newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The government unanimously disagrees with the Social Democratic Party's proposal to lower the retirement age.
- Konsolidacni Banka will contribute 15 billion crowns to the financing of roadways and highways in accord with a government resolution.
- A doctor's strike during the next half year would not make sense, according to David Rath, the chairman of the Doctor's Trade Union.
- Skoda Jaderne Strojirenstvi sro, the largest domestic manufacturer of equipment for nuclear power plants, is applying for a contract with a nuclear power plant in China.
- Chemapol a.s. will hold a general meeting which will concentrate on the question of raising the company's basic capital through the issue of new shares.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Czechs have been depositing significantly less money in banks in the last few months. While from January to April of this year saw an average of five billion crowns being deposited monthly, the average was only two billion between May and August.

- In the first nine months of 1996, 112,000 new cars were sold, a 50 percent increase over the same period in 1995, the greatest increase among European countries. Skoda was once again number one with 60,708 cars sold, 54 percent of the market, In the same period 109,000 used automobiles were imported.
- Skoda's new automobile line, the Octavia was awarded best car of 1997 in Denmark, the first time in recent history Skoda has won such a title abroad.
PRAVO - Twenty-five people, including police officers, soldiers and prison guards, were arrested and accused of extensive fraud on loan applications totalling hundreds of millions of crowns.

- Doctor's wages should increase to three times the national average from the current two times starting in 1998 according to Miroslav Macek of the Health Ministry. He also agreed that nurse's wages should be 1.3 times the average wage.
- The deregulation of energy prices must continue gradually in order to avoid drastic changes and inflation increases, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- SPT Telecom plans to issue seven-year bonds worth a total of seven billion crowns by the end of this year according to Telecom's spokesman, Evzen Stanek.

- Only 17 percent of the computer software used in the Czech Republic was obtained legally according to estimates based on the number of computers and programmes sold. This means that 87 percent of the software used is pirated, costing software dealers billions of crowns yearly.
- The Ministry of Transport will submit an aid proposal to the government to increase the currently stagnant water transport industry.
